title: PMP vs CAPM: Which Project Management Certification First?
dek: Get CAPM if you are new to project management and lack the experience for PMP; get PMP once you have the required experience, because it is the more respected credential and CAPM exempts you from part of its requirements.

seo.metaTitle: PMP vs CAPM: Which Certification First?
seo.metaDescription: PMP vs CAPM compared on cost, experience requirements, and career stage — plus how CAPM can make your later PMP easier.

sources.label: PMI — Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM)

body.richText: Both the PMP and the CAPM come from the Project Management Institute (PMI), but they are aimed at different points in a career. The choice usually comes down to one thing: whether you already have the project experience PMP demands.

Short answer: no qualifying experience yet? Start with CAPM. Have the required experience and want the credential employers ask for by name? Go straight to PMP. CAPM also waives part of the PMP's education requirement later.

body.caption: PMP vs CAPM on the factors that decide which to take first.
rows: None (secondary degree + 23 hours of PM education)
36 months with a 4-year degree, or 60 months with a secondary degree
35 contact hours (waived if you hold an active CAPM)
Working PMs seeking the top credential

body.richText: Holding an active CAPM exempts you from the PMP's 35-contact-hour education requirement later. So for a true beginner, CAPM is not just a consolation prize — it is a stepping stone that reduces friction on the way to PMP.

body.text: When CAPM is the right first choice

items: You are new to project management and cannot yet meet PMP's experience bar
You want a recognized credential to strengthen entry-level applications
You want to lock in the PMP education requirement early via CAPM

body.text: When to go straight to PMP

items: You already have the required months of project experience
You are targeting roles that list PMP by name as a requirement or strong preference
You want the credential with the most hiring recognition and salary leverage

body.richText: Do not chase PMP before you qualify. PMI verifies experience and audits a share of applications. Claiming experience you cannot document risks failing the audit — build the experience first, honestly.

richText: If you have the experience, PMP is the stronger investment and the one employers ask for. If you do not, CAPM gets you moving and makes the PMP easier later. Either way, the credential works best on top of real project experience — see how to build it in

items.question: Should I get CAPM or PMP first?
answerRichText: If you do not yet have the experience PMP requires, get CAPM first. If you do, go straight to PMP — it carries more weight. See the experience bar in

items.question: Is CAPM worth it if I will get PMP later?
items.answerRichText: It can be. CAPM gives newcomers a recognized credential now, and holding an active CAPM exempts you from the PMP's 35-hour education requirement later, reducing your future workload.

items.question: How much do PMP and CAPM cost?
items.answerRichText: As of 2026, the PMP exam is $405 for PMI members and $555 for non-members; CAPM is $225 for members and $300 for non-members. Confirm current fees on PMI's official site before applying.
